fact: ARPCE director general Louis Marc Sakala said on 16 January 2026, closing a Brazzaville seminar on digital technology policy and regulation, that the seminar was about how to 'define' (définir) the country's digital economy strategy; no adoption or validation is stated.

Telecom Review Africa, on 17 October 2025, calls Congo's Digital Strategy 2030 'upcoming' and 'developed with World Bank support', describing it as the nation's long-term vision for digital sovereignty and innovation; no adoption is stated.

Minister of Posts, Telecommunications and the Digital Economy Léon Juste Ibombo announced on 13 October 2025 that the Digital Strategy 2030 document was complete and under review by the government's general secretariat before submission to the Head of State for final approval by decree.
The article says the Digital Strategy 2030 document was completed with World Bank financial support; it states no domestic budget line for it.

The Digital Strategy 2030, a decade roadmap covering digital public services, connectivity, youth digital skills, cybersecurity, AI and digital sovereignty, was reported complete on 13 October 2025 and moved to government secretariat review ahead of adoption by decree.

A national workshop opened by the Minister of Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Economy in Brazzaville in July 2025 to outline a digital identity roadmap was described as a milestone in implementing Congo Digital 2025, the national strategy for digital technology as a catalyst for inclusive and sustainable development; the article gives its publication date of 21 July 2025 and no event day.

The World Bank appraisal says the Government of Congo had adopted a five-year Digital Economy Strategy, 'Vision Congo Digital 2025'; it names no adopting act or date, so the date used is the document's own, 11 May 2022.

The appraisal says the Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Economy is mandated to implement the national digital transformation agenda, an inter-ministerial digital sector strategic committee coordinates the strategy, and the Directorate General for Digital Economy Development is commissioned to operationalise it across ministries; the date used is the document's own, 11 May 2022.

The appraisal says successful implementation of the strategy requires a clear and prioritised roadmap, and the project's results framework includes validation of digital transformation strategy action plans as an indicator to be achieved; no action plan is described as existing; the date used is the document's own, 11 May 2022.
The appraisal says successful implementation of the strategy requires monitoring and evaluation mechanisms, which it does not describe as in place; the date used is the document's own, 11 May 2022.

The World Bank digital economy diagnostic says the Republic of Congo adopted in June 2019 the national strategy for the digital economy 'Vision Congo Digital 2025', whose three pillars are citizen services, digitalisation of government and development of the private digital sector.

The diagnostic says the Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Economy led the drafting and the digital programme, and that the Directorate General for Digital Economy Development was recently set up to lead implementation of the national digital strategy; a draft decree for a permanent inter-institutional digital development committee had been submitted. No month is given, so the diagnostic's own date, December 2020, is used.

The diagnostic says the Directorate General is mandated to implement an action plan arising from the strategy, which was still being drawn up with consultants under the CAB project, and that implementation plans needed to be articulated with defined roles for each stakeholder; the diagnostic's own date, December 2020, is used.

Décret n° 2019-150 of 17 June 2019, published in the Journal officiel of 4 July 2019, approves the national strategy for the development of the digital economy; the held passages do not describe the strategy's contents beyond calling for new bodies such as ANSSI, so its coverage of the state is not shown.

The held text of the 2019 Journal officiel says the Directorate General for Digital Economy Development is charged with implementing the national digital policy and that further bodies, starting with the national information systems security agency ANSSI, need to be created; dated to the Journal officiel's publication, 4 July 2019.

Following its mid-term review, the PATN steering committee recommended proposing a date for validation by the Council of Ministers of the strategy "Vision Congo digital 2030"; the article gives no adoption. The review date is not stated, so the article's publication date is used.
The strategy is named "Vision Congo digital 2030".

The ITU repository lists the National Digital Development Plan (PNDN) as the country's strategy and says the countries it lists have adopted one; no adopting act is named, so this is dated by the repository's 2025 publication year.
The repository gives the time frame of the National Digital Development Plan (PNDN) as 2021 - 2025.
The repository names the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications as lead/owner of the National Digital Development Plan (PNDN).

Convergence Afrique reports that the national digital transformation strategy 'Congo Digital 2025' was launched by the government in August 2019 to guarantee equitable access to digital services for all citizens by 2025.
Minister Léon Juste Ibombo said on 13 October 2025 that the Stratégie numérique 2030 is finalised with World Bank financial support but needs the government's official approval to unlock financing.
